sources.title: Human History Map 4000 BCE borders

sources.title: Human History Map 3000 BCE borders

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 BCE borders

sources.title: Is There Such a Thing as Hunter-Gatherer Archaeology?
sources.note: Peer-reviewed methodological review checked for the category’s history, diversity, colonial baggage, partially shared features, and limits of treating foragers as one social type.

sources.title: Genetic history from the Middle Neolithic to present on Sardinia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ancient-genome study checked for 70 individuals, Neolithic farmer affinity, Chalcolithic and Bronze Age continuity, regional isolation, and limits of ancestry labels.

sources.title: Stone tools and foraging in northern Madagascar challenge Holocene extinction models
sources.note: Peer-reviewed claim checked for microliths, rockshelter context, OSL ages extending before 2000 BCE, coastal foraging, and the proposed early human presence.

sources.title: New evidence of megafaunal bone damage indicates late colonization of Madagascar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment checked for bioturbation, cutmark tests, absent early tools and settlements, and a much later 1350 to 1100 BP colonization estimate.

sources.title: History of the necropolis of Li Muri: The Neolithic
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for Neolithic agriculture, livestock, stable settlements, stone tools, and pottery in Sardinia.

sources.title: Ozieri, Grotta di San Michele
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for the 3200 to 2800 BCE Ozieri phase, cave reuse, habitation, cult, burial, huts, villages, and ceramics.

sources.title: Funerary Tradition in the Prehistory of Sardinia: the domus de janas
sources.note: UNESCO documentation checked for fifth- to third-millennium rock-cut tombs, settlement proximity, house imitation, motifs, social change, and early Bronze Age transition.

sources.title: Alghero, Necropolis of Anghelu Ruju
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for thirty-eight tombs, collective burial, grave goods, home-like architectural details, offerings, ochre, and 3200 to 1600 BCE use.

sources.title: Eneolithic Sardinia
sources.note: Regional heritage overview checked for Copper Age mining and metallurgy, settlement and mortuary change, and increasing social, political, and economic complexity.

sources.title: Monte Claro archaeological context
sources.note: Official cultural catalogue checked for the 2400 to 2100 BCE Monte Claro phase, burial context, human remains, and characteristic ceramic vessels.

sources.title: Was there mid Holocene habitation in Madagascar? A reconsideration
sources.note: Peer-reviewed critique checked for the claimed 4500 BP rockshelter dates, extensive bioturbation, over-dispersed OSL results, and chronological uncertainty.

sources.title: Bonnanaro, Necropolis of Corona Moltana
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for early Bronze Age Bonnanaro chronology, long tomb use, chambers, niches, carved cups, and cultural transition.

sources.title: Diversity of forager lifeways in the prehistoric past
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review checked for prehistoric forager diversity, missing modern analogues, and the need to model rather than clone ethnographic communities.

sources.title: A critical review of radiocarbon dates clarifies the human settlement of Madagascar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology review checked for divergent colonization estimates, contextual weakness of early cutmarked bones, and the unusually unresolved settlement timeline.

sources.title: Patterns of late Holocene and historical extinctions on Madagascar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis checked for hydroclimate, floral and faunal records, Lakaton chronology, later hearth dates, and competing climate-human explanations.

sources.title: Madagascar: A History of Arrivals, What Happened, and Will Happen Next
sources.note: Scholarly review checked for varied landscapes, unpredictable climate, multiple arrivals, settlement debate, introduced biota, and ecological transformation.

sources.title: Domus de janas nomination: Scientific Insights
sources.note: UNESCO expert documentation checked for thousands of tombs across varied Sardinian environments, settlements, monuments, pottery, and archaeological interpretive limits.

sources.title: North-eastern Sardinia under changing Holocene climates and land use
sources.note: Peer-reviewed palaeoenvironmental study checked for Holocene vegetation, probabilistic land-use reconstruction, climate variation, and the need to compare environmental and archaeological evidence.

sources.title: Patterns of late Holocene and historical extinctions on Madagascar, open text
sources.note: Peer-reviewed open synthesis checked for wet and dry regional differences, last-four-millennia hydroclimate, extinct fauna, and separating human from climatic drivers.

sources.title: Origins and spread of agriculture in Sardinia: prehistoric plant remains
sources.note: University research record checked for domesticated cereals and legumes, crop processing, agrarian practice, and plant-based reconstruction of farming communities.

sources.title: Crop and wild plant exploitation at Su Mulinu Mannu, Sardinia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed university record checked for the 4500 to 4100 cal BCE sampled context, Middle Neolithic wheat, naked and hulled barley, wild plants, and site-specific limits.

sources.title: The role of pottery in Middle Neolithic Sardinia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for its 4500 to 4000 cal BCE contexts, pottery form and use-wear, biomolecular methods, ruminant fats, plant foods, non-ruminant products, and aquatic resources.

sources.title: Prehistoric Italian foodways: stable-isotope meta-analysis
sources.note: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis checked for 1590 plant, animal, and human measurements, terrestrial protein, C3 plants, Copper Age variation, and dietary-inference limits.

sources.title: Animal products in the Mediterranean Copper Age: Scaba e Arriu
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Sardinian study checked for burial phases about 3400 to 2600 and 2700 to 2350 BCE, human and animal isotopes, livestock, animal-product use, and climate context.

sources.title: Obsidian in prehistoric Sardinia
sources.note: Regional heritage synthesis checked for Monte Arci sources, extraction and processing locations, blades and other tools, distribution, exchange debate, and production sequence.

sources.title: Sassari, prehistoric altar of Monte d’Accoddi
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for the 3200 to 2600 BCE sequence, first altar, rebuilding, later village huts, ramp, plastered shrine, necropolis, and building materials.

sources.title: The bronzetti and Sardinian metallurgy
sources.note: Regional heritage account checked for Copper Age antecedents, copper and lead extraction, later bronze alloying, tools, ornaments, and explicit chronological separation.

sources.title: Art and Architecture in the Prehistory of Sardinia
sources.note: UNESCO nomination documentation checked for tombs, menhirs, dolmens, caves, sanctuaries, settlements, motifs, and coexisting hypogeal and megalithic practices.

sources.title: Mitogenome Diversity in Sardinians: A Genetic Window onto an Island’s Past
sources.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study checked for 21 prehistoric mitogenomes, Neolithic-to-Bronze sampling, island diversity, chronology, and limits of population continuity inferences.

sources.title: Complete mitochondrial sequences from Mesolithic Sardinia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ancient-DNA study checked for two roughly 10,000-year-old individuals, scarce pre-Neolithic remains, later migration, and the small contribution inferred for those lineages.

sources.title: Genomic history of the Sardinian population
sources.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study checked for modern within-island structure, early farmer affinity, Neolithic replacement model, and caution against equating ancestry with a named culture.

sources.title: How Do Hunter-Gatherer Children Learn Subsistence Skills?
sources.note: Peer-reviewed meta-ethnography checked for definitional diversity, observation, participation, play, teaching, peer learning, skill timelines, and uneven study of gathering and domestic work.

sources.title: Cultural transmission among hunter-gatherers
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review checked for diverse learning pathways, early transmission of everyday skills, intergenerational and peer teaching, and intercultural variation.

sources.title: Child and adolescent time allocation in twelve forager societies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparative study checked for cross-cultural variation in play, childcare, domestic work, learning, food production, and safe-resource collection.

sources.title: Harsh environments promote alloparental care across human societies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparative study checked for cooperative childcare, reciprocity, environmental risk, and broad variation rather than a universal household formula.

sources.title: Mobility and kinship in the world’s first village societies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis checked for mobility, kinship, domestic architecture, ritual, managed and wild foods, and non-linear change between foraging and farming.

sources.title: Paleoparasitology of historical toilets and mummies in South Korea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed South Korean review checked for no identified Neolithic toilet structures there, coprolites in middens, parasite evidence, and the strictly comparative scope of that record.

sources.title: The Nora stele, oldest written document in Sardinia
sources.note: National museum account checked for the Phoenician inscription, disputed translation, 850 to 725 BCE date, and its status as Sardinia’s earliest written document.

sources.title: Genomic landscape of human diversity across Madagascar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for heterogeneous African and Asian ancestry, independent movements, island-wide diversity, and much later Malagasy population history.

sources.title: Austronesian-Bantu admixture and cultural reversion in a Madagascar forager group
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study checked for Mikea mixed ancestry, recent subsistence change, Malagasy context, and why modern foragers are not relics of a prehistoric population.

sources.title: The Bonnanaro phase at Thomes
sources.note: Regional heritage chronology checked for Bonnanaro A and B, 1800 to 1500 BCE transition, funerary sites, and early corridor nuraghi.

sources.title: A small cohort of Island Southeast Asian women founded Madagascar
sources.note: Peer-reviewed genetic study checked for later Austronesian connections, broad archaeological and linguistic bounds, uncertainty, and the much later chronology than this atlas interval.

sources.title: Settling Madagascar: when did people first colonise the world’s largest island?
sources.note: University archaeology summary checked for disputed early cutmarks and stone tools, settlement chronology, methodological debate, and the distinction between a visit and sustained colonization.

proposedOverrides.name: Atlas “Hunters-gatherers” category: Sardinia and Madagascar
proposedOverrides.summary: An atlas catch-all that colors Madagascar and Sardinia together, despite settled Sardinian farming communities and sharply disputed evidence for human presence in Madagascar during the mapped interval.
